subject: gov.policy
name: ADIGE digital agenda

position_start: The stated digital agenda, with the diagnostic's recommendations outstanding
position_end: Launched 2019 by the Ministerio de Transportes, Correos y Telecomunicaciones on 33 lineas de accion running to 2025, aligned with the UN 2030 Agenda SDGs, the CPLP Digital Agenda and the African Union's Agenda 2063; unchanged since - no implementation report, budget figure or revised agenda is held

subject: gov.policy
name: Consolidated July-December 2026 action plan
milestone: Adopted by the second extraordinary directive council, 31 July 2026, and not yet financed
position_end: Adopted with 35 strategic objectives under three national priorities, one of them restoring sovereignty over the national digital space; it goes to the interministerial council and then to the Council of Ministers, which decides what is recorded and funded
note: the plan document is not published; the government portal dates the council to 31 July and Real Equatorial Guinea to 30 July

subject: gov.policy
name: Governance of state-participation companies
milestone: Directorships filled by competitive interview with six-month provisional appointments
position_start: Appointments and board membership not on record as contested
position_end: Article 16 of the Ley Reguladora de Empresas Publicas invoked to remove supervising officeholders from parastatal boards, and director-general posts at GITGE, ANDEGE, INSESO and Gepetrol Servicios filled by competitive interview against stated criteria

subject: gov.policy
name: Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2035
milestone: The framework the World Bank Country Economic Memorandum assesses
position_start: In force as the national development framework
position_end: In force; primary text recovered (Agenda Guinea Ecuatorial 2035 / ENDS 2035, successor to the Plan Horizonte 2020, no internal adoption date, uploaded 2024-05) commits to gradual privatisation of state telecom ownership, universal broadband backbone across all regions, an updated telecoms legal and regulatory framework, and a proposed Fondo de Apoyo a la Ciencia, Tecnologia e Innovacion (FACTI) that may be funded by a special tax on oil and gas exports; the World Bank's separately noted digital recommendations - a one-stop shop, online business registration and a digitised commercial registry - remain undelivered on record

subject: gov.legislate

subject: gov.legislate
name: Reform of the Ley de Prensa y Medios Audiovisuales (1997)
milestone: Information Minister presented the reform bill to the Chamber of Deputies, 6 August 2026, referred to the Public Works and Communication committee
position_start: In force since 1997, with no provision for digital media or cable TV
position_end: Bill presented adding regulation of digital media and cable television for the first time, under committee review, with no adoption date or bill text published; a separate Copyright and Related Rights bill was presented alongside it, implementing Equatorial Guinea's 1997 Berne Convention accession and its 2015 Bangui Agreement obligations under OAPI
note: neither bill text is held; scope is as reported from the minister's appearance. The copyright provisions are a companion bill rather than part of the audiovisual bill, which the earlier record did not separate

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law and supervisory authority
milestone: Gazetted 22 July 2016, in force twenty days later
position_end: In force since 2016-08-11; gives rights of access, rectification, cancellation, opposition and indemnisation and a sanctions regime running to CFA 15,000,000 for the gravest infractions, but Article 15 leaves the Organo Rector de Proteccion de Datos Personales - and the registry it would run - to a decree the government has never issued; africadataprotection.org's own country page records no supervisory authority publicly identified
note: the Organo Rector was never created by the decree Article 15 requires

subject: gov.regional
name: Lusophone Africa data governance process
milestone: Second Lusophone Africa Data Governance Workshop, Luanda, 15-17 June 2026
position_end: Participated at the second regional workshop applying UNESCO's Data Governance Toolkit; no national framework or commitment resulted on the record

subject: gov.regional
name: Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection
milestone: Signed at Addis Ababa, 28 July 2026
position_start: Neither signed nor ratified, per the African Union register as at 2026-02-02
position_end: Signatory since 28 July 2026 and not a party; no instrument of ratification is on file or on the AU register
note: the Chamber of Deputies' unanimous vote of 25 March 2026 was a domestic authorisation to ratify, taken before the country was a signatory

subject: gov.standards
